notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

itch.io games: link your itch.io account on the console's web page (PC Games/Apps, itch.io, Link itch.io) and sign in on itch.io. The games you own that have a Linux ARM64 build, or a LOVE file, can then be added to the console, each as its own tile on the Ports and Apps tab that starts the game straight away. Home, the pause menu and Quit work as for any port. SCCM Retro's picks are listed there too, free games checked on a console: Cro-Mag Rally, Celeste 64, Otto Matic, Bugdom and Nanosaur, each added with one press. A paid game needs buying on itch.io first. You can also link with an itch.io API key instead of signing in.

Bluetooth controllers keep their port by their Bluetooth address instead of their name, the way paired Joy-Cons already did. Two controllers of the same kind, like two Pro Controllers, each keep their own port whatever else is connected.

Standalone PPSSPP: L and R work on consoles where PPSSPP had never saved its controls. The launcher now sets up PPSSPP's own default controls, with L and R, before the first launch.

RAM tuner: when the fastest speed that passed the quick test failed the long one, the tuner skipped the speed just under it (2800 after 2833 failed, in one report). It now tries that speed next. If yours finished lower than you expected, running it again may find more.

New and lightly tested: the itch.io sign-in and adding a free game were checked with one account; updating a game and paid games are not checked yet. Bluetooth controller ports were checked with stand-ins, not real Bluetooth controllers. PPSSPP's L and R were set up on a console but not pressed in a game yet. The RAM tuner fix was checked in the tuner's own test, not a real run.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
